solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After restraint, finding outlet for being creative again

blocks.note: a rein holds a horse back
venting feelings is finding an outlet for them

explanation.surface: Someone held back for a while finally lets off steam and starts making new things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After restraint' places the venting after the rein, giving REINVENTING.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvent is to devise something anew, so reinventing is being inventive a second time.

clue.text: Legendary winger not using all of pitch

indicators.note: leaving part unused means a letter is dropped from the word that follows

blocks.note: a ship pitches or rocks in a swell

explanation.surface: A footballer of legend who doesn't cover the whole field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer, but here it is a bird; ROCK loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian tales, a creature of legend with wings.

clue.text: Admission from one who's pushing a principle

blocks.note: a drug pusher confessing their trade, read as two words, a pronoun then a verb

explanation.surface: A confession from someone pressing a particular belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing' here means peddling drugs, and the dealer's admission is 'I deal', read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a guiding standard or value one holds to, much like a principle.

clue.text: Break for taking photos: this is in shot?

blocks.note: short for vacation, a break from study
a cine camera takes moving photographs

explanation.surface: A holiday spent snapping pictures, with the subject posing in frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests photography, but the definition means an injection.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine is the substance delivered in a jab, which is commonly called a shot.

clue.text: Gaining nothing from turning snippet of film into porn

indicators.note: a snippet is a tiny clipping, here only the opening letter of the next word
turning one thing into another suggests the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of film
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film-maker earns nothing by converting a clip into pornography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link to the conversion but its letters join the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonprofit organisation is set up not to make money, so it gains nothing financially.

clue.text: Small picture contains etching, somewhat reduced

indicators.note: both words are trimmed down, so only a stretch of the letters across them is kept

blocks.note: the tail of contains runs into the start of etching

explanation.surface: A miniature that includes an etching shrunk to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contains' looks like the signal for a hidden word, but it is itself part of the letters searched.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small illustration set within a larger page or map.

clue.text: Indulge in golf with light keep fit, climbing

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word wraps around the other
in a down entry, climbing means reading upward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ray is a beam of light
taken as written

explanation.surface: Treat yourself on the golf course with some gentle exercise involving going uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep fit' looks like one phrase of exercise, but 'keep' is the container signal and only 'fit' climbs, inside the light.
explanation.definitionFit: To gratify is to satisfy or pander to a desire, which is what indulging means.

clue.text: Inappropriate to beg for seat

blocks.note: first meaning: to cadge, as in asking for a cigarette
second meaning: slang for the backside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inappropriate' also fits the word as slang adjective (a wrong or bad thing), making this almost a triple definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word means both to scrounge something from someone and one's bottom, the part one sits on.

clue.text: Writer of book everyone aims to follow

blocks.note: B is an abbreviation for book
all means everyone
to point a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: An author whose book everybody tries to imitate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint pen is an instrument for writing, so it is a writer in the literal sense.

clue.text: Playing small part in track race and not fit

indicators.note: placing one item in another means its letters sit inside the second word

blocks.note: the mile is a classic race on the running track
nor means and not
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: An unfit athlete has only a small role in the running race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fit' looks like a phrase meaning unwell, but 'not' pairs with 'and' while 'fit' stands alone as a bout of fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor-league describes something second-rate or of lesser importance, like a team in a lower division.

clue.text: Not exactly concerned with odours in suburban streets?

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, meaning about or approximately
re means regarding
scents are smells

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely worried about smells in the suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescents are curved residential roads, typical of suburban housing estates; the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Character in Lewis inclined to leave tip

indicators.note: the tip here is the end letter, which is told to go away

blocks.note: aslant means at a slope

explanation.surface: A figure on the Isle of Lewis tempted to skip a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis could be the Hebridean island, but it is the author C. S. Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslan is the great lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books, a character created by that author.

clue.text: My hosts left pork pie for worker of mine

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the outer word holds the others

blocks.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
L is the abbreviation for left
rhyming slang: pork pie means a lie

explanation.surface: Someone offers guests a pork pie left out for a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a falsehood, and 'my!' is the exclamation cor, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, someone who works in a pit or mine.

clue.text: Some needlework clubs, most equipped with IT, at church

blocks.note: C stands for clubs in card notation
the most capable
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Sewing groups at a church have been kitted out with computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable stitch is a knitting pattern resembling twisted rope, a kind of decorative needlework.

clue.text: Excursionist originally travelling first class down under

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of travelling
Australian slang for something excellent

explanation.surface: A tourist who began their journey flying first class in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' means Australia, where ripper is everyday praise for something first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a person on a short pleasure trip or day excursion.

clue.text: One sounding retreat after advance of large German battle formation

indicators.note: the letter is pushed forward and slotted in earlier in the word

blocks.note: a bugle sounds the call to retreat
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bugler signals withdrawal once a big German advance is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: The L in BUGLE moves forward one place, swapping with the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulge is a salient pushed into enemy lines, as in the 1944 German offensive, the Battle of the Bulge.

clue.text: Work with diet, perhaps, on one's behind

blocks.note: in cricket, the on side is also called the leg side
I (one) plus 's
behind time means late

explanation.surface: Someone working on their diet to slim their rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' suggests food, but it is a parliament such as Japan's Diet; in cricket the on side and leg side are the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, and to legislate is to make laws, the work such a body does.

clue.text: Rebellion and a number of revolutions, once

blocks.note: first meaning: the Jacobite rising of 1745
second meaning: the speed in rpm of an old single record

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutions' pretends to continue the theme of rebellion, but means turns of a record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobite uprising of 1745 is called the 'Forty-Five', and singles once played at that many revolutions per minute.

clue.text: Like some elements far from well done — huge cost?

blocks.note: rare steak is lightly cooked
to cost the earth is to be very expensive

explanation.surface: An undercooked steak at an outrageous price.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare-earth elements are a group of metals such as the lanthanides, so the term describes certain chemical elements.

clue.text: US aircraft whisking one away?

blocks.note: first meaning: American slang for a helicopter
second meaning: a whisk, which beats eggs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Whisking away' suggests being flown off, but the tool whisks an egg, the 'one' being whisked.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-beater is a kitchen whisk, and in US slang the word also names a helicopter for its whirling rotors.

clue.text: Rotten old peach, days out of date

indicators.note: rotten fruit is spoiled and broken down, so these letters are jumbled
out means taken away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: An ancient peach, past its use-by date, has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of date' reads as one phrase, but 'out' removes D from OLD PEACH and 'of date' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means relating to an epoch, a particular point or period in time, hence a date.

clue.text: Tag in new sort of suit for taking off?

definitions.text: sort of suit for taking off?

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A label in a new suit that you tear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests undressing, but it means flight; pilots wear such suits against acceleration forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-g suit is a pressurised garment that stops jet pilots blacking out during high-acceleration manoeuvres.

clue.text: Type of novel, something delightful, then again, too short

indicators.note: excessively shortened means more than one end letter is cut away

blocks.note: a gas is informal for great fun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of book that is a joy, but once more ends too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: AGAIN loses its last two letters. An Aga saga is a British genre of novel about comfortable middle-class country life; an Aga is a big range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga saga is the name for a genre of domestic fiction, so it is one type of novel.

clue.text: Replaced scythe, originally ok, cuts some grass

indicators.note: things replaced are put back differently, so these letters change places
originally points to the beginning, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: first letter of scythe
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new scythe, fine at first, mows some of the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' reads as the verb of mowing but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense clump or tuft of grass.

clue.text: Buzzer tip for quick answer at end of quiz rounds

indicators.note: the tip of a word is taken here as its far end, a single letter
the end is the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: last letter of quick
A is the abbreviation for answer
last letter of quiz
two rounds, two Os

explanation.surface: Advice on hitting the buzzer quickly at the end of quiz rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' and 'quick answer' paint a quiz show, but the buzzer is a toy instrument; 'tip' looks like the first letter but is the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A kazoo is a toy instrument that makes a buzzing sound when you hum into it.

clue.text: Old enough to be a model

blocks.note: ex means former
ample means sufficient

explanation.surface: Someone now mature enough to work as a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a pattern to copy, which is one sense of model.

clue.text: One thing most favoured, the other less important

blocks.note: a pet project or subject is a favourite
'the other' and 'it' are both euphemisms for sex

explanation.surface: Of two things, one is cherished and the other matters less.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit, as in petit bourgeois or petit point, means small or minor, of lesser importance.

clue.text: Refuse request ultimately not considered

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final position, so only the end letter is used

blocks.note: last letter of request
rash means done without thought

explanation.surface: A request is turned down because it was never thought about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is rubbish or waste, which is what refuse means as a noun.

clue.text: Prophet brought back a light weight chicken for dinner?

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so it reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: an ounce, abbreviated oz, is a small weight
a roaster is a bird bred for roasting

explanation.surface: A seer returns with a small portion of roast chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoroaster, also called Zarathustra, was the ancient Persian prophet who founded Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: Fine US broadcaster in need of satellite

indicators.note: being in need of something means lacking it, so those letters are missing

blocks.note: a radio broadcasts
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: An excellent American station that requires a satellite link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rad is American slang for excellent or cool, so it means fine in US usage.

clue.text: An aspect of Chaucer regularly overlooked

indicators.note: skipping at regular intervals means every other letter is ignored

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A facet of Chaucer's work that is often ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Hue can mean a character or complexion, as in an opinion of a different hue, so it is an aspect.

clue.text: Brave, like multimillionairesses

definitions.note: cryptic: the word has LION at its exact centre

blocks.note: first meaning: courageous
second meaning, cryptic: the twenty-letter word has LION as its middle four letters

explanation.walkthrough: Look at the long word itself: multimil-LION-airesses has a lion at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the courage of a lion is the plain sense; the word multimillionairesses literally has a lion at its heart.
